Laura — attaching my interim notes (latency_spike_analysis.xlsx). Quick summary:

- Two significant 99th percentile spikes on May 28 and May 31, both originating in us-west-2.
- Root cause (prelim): a change to batching behavior when sequence-length distribution shifted for a high-volume customer test. The runtime failed to re-optimize kernels fast enough for the shorter sequences, leading to CPU-side scheduling delays.
- Mitigation: forced fallback to previous kernel selection and a hotfix to the batch-size estimation logic. We saw tail latency normalize within 30 minutes after rollback.

Action items I need: logs from the test customer for the May 28 run (Grace, can you confirm which customer/infra test was in us-west-2 that day?). I'll convert this to one slide for the QBR deck and mark the RCA status (draft -> final) by Monday EOD.

-Karthik

Laura / team — attaching the cost export (cost_by_model_20270606.csv). Quick notes: 

- May overrun ~8% vs forecast; majority driven by two items: (1) burst usage on hosted endpoints for the enterprise sandbox tier, and (2) an unanticipated dedicated capacity spin-up we didn't fully offset with auto-scale policies.
- Reserved commitments are still within expected thresholds but the burst buffer usage is the marginal cost driver.
- Suggested deck language: show run-rate + one-off items and proposed mitigations (tighten burst throttles, adjust autoscale thresholds, and review per-tenant caching TTLs).

I'll prepare a slide with a straightforward 3-point ask for Nimbus: (a) confirm expected growth for sandbox usage, (b) discuss a modest reserved uplift vs seasonality, (c) alignment on caching expectations to lower token/unit usage.
